bridge.rule: No net successor forecast or offset without evidenced overlap allocation. Existing corporate facilities are retained, not relabeled as data-center cost.

exclusions: Business-product engineering and J2 faculty payroll already in business/J2 models
Core Finance/Legal/People/Facilities/physical-security staffing outside quantified technology pool
Premiums, banking transaction fees, general counsel/tax/external audit fees and matter-specific external specialists
Industrial production/transport/refining/assay contracts and original asset costs
Taxes, financing costs, land appreciation, terminal asset sale proceeds and construction schedule financing
Full training campus / office construction and hospitality
Vendor-specific licensing bundles, committed-spend discounts, actual quotes and negotiated support SLAs
notes: All alternatives include the same logical service demand and retained enterprise tooling; the restricted estate and local site hardware remain internally controlled.
Recovery is counted once through derived workload fractions. Backups are separately sized; RTO/RPO remain unproven.
Discounted cash is a comparison metric, not a valuation or investment authorization. No terminal proceeds are assumed; closing net book value is reported separately.
Hardware capacity expands with modeled demand; prior cohorts refresh after 48 months. Depreciation begins the following month.
Demand growth is not evidence that the current workforce has spare capacity. Workload-hours and reuse assumptions require staffed validation.
Offline backup price covers illustrative media/handling only, not proof of an offline copy.
Industrial 140 + 131 staffing is held constant only for this 2027 license-seat scenario; those source populations are not relabeled as an approved 2027 payroll.
All 606 Core occupied scenario positions are assumed to need full-service licenses; the 271 industrial positions are assumed to use a frontline mix. Neither license mix is an observed inventory.

Quantified staffing is fractional delivery capacity, not an immediately approved number of hires. Dedicated unshared staffing rounds each skill pool up separately. Reuse sensitivities assume cross-qualified sharing and are lower bounds.

Variable workload effort scales with the square root of the central 25% annual demand-growth assumption; 65% of effort is modeled as fixed. This is an editable modeling convention, not an empirical staffing law.

Local/site hardware is an aggregate costing envelope, not a per-installation resilient OT design. Existing site communications, per-site redundancy and safety-system engineering remain outside this cost comparison.
